info.name: Go Server: App API
info.description:
Everything the app can call on the Go Server. Import this file and the environment file into Postman.

**Run it end to end:** start `pnpm dev:stack`, then run the folder *Run in order* (Collection Runner, or `pnpm postman`). It signs up two people, makes a trip and goes through every route, checking each answer.

**Reference folders** hold one request per route with saved example answers. Run *Create person*, then *Create trip*, and every other request uses `{{token}}` and `{{tripId}}` automatically. Votes, mandates, record lines and Go's cards are made by Go, so their ids come from the *[Go]* requests in *Run in order*.

Errors always look like `{"error": {"code", "message"}}`. Money is whole paise. Full reference: docs/API.md.

item.name: Run in order
item.description: The whole app API end to end, with checks on every answer. Start the local stack first (`pnpm dev:stack`: a temporary Postgres, a fake Go and the real server), then run this folder in order: in Postman with the Collection Runner, or `pnpm postman`. Requests marked **[Go]** act as Go through the stack's control port (`{{simUrl}}`), for what only Go can do: open a vote, set a mandate, post a card, write a record line, ask for a spend approval. Each run makes new people and a new trip, so it can be run again and again.

item.name: Reference: 2. Messages
item.description: Chat. Every post needs your own `client_id` so retries never post twice.

query.description: Return messages with updated_seq greater than this

request.description: Messages posted **or changed** after a change number, oldest change first. Page on: next `after_seq` = last message's `updated_seq`. A reaction without `person_id` is Go's. `author.kind:"go"` messages must look like Go, never a person.

originalRequest.description: Messages posted **or changed** after a change number, oldest change first. Page on: next `after_seq` = last message's `updated_seq`. A reaction without `person_id` is Go's. `author.kind:"go"` messages must look like Go, never a person.

request.description:
`client_id` is **required** (use a new UUID per press; the same id again returns the first answer). Send `text` (≤4000) and/or `attachments` (≤10).

- `reply_to`: message id being replied to.
- `about_message_id`: **"Ask Go about this"** (Go answers even if the text doesn't name Go).
- `mentions`: person ids (≤30).
- Attachments: `{kind:"photo",url,width?,height?,caption?}` or `{kind:"file",url,name,mime,size_bytes}` (URLs only, no upload yet).

The message counts as *for Go* when it has `@Go`, starts with "Go,", replies to Go, or has `about_message_id`.

**Saves `messageId`.**

item.name: Reference: 4. Asking Go (via the Server)

item.name: Reference: 6. Live connection (SSE)
item.description: Postman can open this but is awkward for streams; in the app use a streaming HTTP client.

request.description:
`text/event-stream`, with the `Authorization` header (browser `EventSource` can't send it). `: ping` every 20 s.

| event | data | do |
|---|---|---|
| `hello` | `{trip_id}` | connected |
| `message` | full Message | add/replace by `message_id` (also edits, deletes, reactions, **replaced cards**) |
| `trip` | `{seq}` | re-read the trip + needs-you if `seq` is higher than yours |
| `typing` | `{who, on, until?}` | show/hide "Go is typing..." |

After a reconnect, re-read messages (`after_seq`) and the trip.
